h1: Do I need a permit for a patio or walkway in Newton, MA?
title: Newton Patio and Walkway Permits: Site Plans, Drainage and Historic Review
description: Learn why patio and walkway work can involve Engineering, zoning, stormwater, and historic review even when no building is constructed.
short_answer: A patio or walkway is not automatically covered by the state building-code exemption for sidewalks and driveways. Newton Engineering reviews expansions of impervious surface, including patios, and grade alterations. Properties in a Local Historic District also need historic review for exterior hardscaping changes.

facts.text: Newton Engineering reviews site plans for expansions of impervious area, including patios, and for grade alterations.
Newton's stormwater ordinance identifies certain new impervious-area projects and land-disturbance projects as requiring stormwater review.
Newton requires a Historic District Application for exterior changes, including walkways and hardscaping, at properties in its Local Historic Districts.

qa.q: Does the state driveway exemption automatically cover a patio?
qa.a: No. The cited state exemption names sidewalks and driveways, not patios. Confirm the permit requirements for the proposed patio with Newton.
